title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is comparing the modular multiplicities (analytic stacks) M_{1,1} and M_{0,4} ≃ U_{0,3}. U_{0,3} is the universal curve of type (0,3), i.e. P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, with S_3 acting by permuting the punctures. On the previous page he obtained only an exterior (outer) homomorphism T^+_{1,1} → S^+_{0,3} induced by M_{1,1} → (U_{0,3}, S_3). He asked whether it can be refined to an actual homomorphism, not just an outer one. This page answers yes, using the Teichmüller space.

1. Teichmüller space and (74). The Teichmüller space of M_{1,1} is the Poincaré half-plane D (§38), viewed as a canonical universal cover. Relative to it one gets a genuine isomorphism (74) π_1(M_{1,1}^an) ≃ SL(2,Z), 'not merely exterior'. This is essentially his earlier (50); the orientation-preserving T^+_{1,1} is the index-2 subgroup of T_{1,1} ≅ GL(2,Z).

2. The map (75). There is a canonical map D → U_{0,3}^an ≃ M_{1,1}[2]', the level-2 modular curve rigidified by ±1. This is the classical Legendre λ-function H → P^1 \ {0,1,∞}.

3. Equivariance (76). The map is equivariant along SL(2,Z)' = PSL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/2) ≃ S_3. The kernel Γ(2)/±1 is free of rank 2, i.e. π_{0,3}.

4. Conclusion. D is thus a universal covering of the multiplicity (U_{0,3}^an, S_3), the orbifold P^1 \ {0,1,∞} // S_3. PSL(2,Z) is its 'mixed' (equivariant) fundamental group, which is the π_1 of the quotient stack.

5. Base point. To identify this group with π_1((U_{0,3}, S_3); P = -J̄) one must choose a point of D above P = -J̄ = e^{iπ/3}, the Z/3-fixed point. The choice is ambiguous up to the free kernel π_{0,3}. The next page picks J = e^{2πi/3} and checks that it lies over P and not over P̄; the three matrices sending J to -J̄ there are correct.

Purpose: fix canonical, non-outer identifications between the Teichmüller groups of type (1,1) and (0,4)/(0,3) with S_3 symmetry. These are base-point choices at the tangential/symmetric point, needed for the Galois action on the first levels of the Teichmüller tower (the 'équation des lacets').
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The machine reading '(par auto. extérieurs)' would wrongly suggest only an outer isomorphism; the image reads 'pas seulement extérieur', which is correct for the stack M_{1,1} with Teichmüller base point D.
The § and page number for the explicit iso SL(2,Z/2) ≃ S_3 is left blank (an unfinished cross-reference).

ideas.what: Teichmüller space of type (1,1) = upper half-plane as canonical universal cover, giving a genuine (not outer) isomorphism π_1(M_{1,1}^an) ≃ SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: M_{1,1}^an = [H/SL(2,Z)] as an analytic orbifold/stack; orbifold fundamental group SL(2,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Teichmüller); stack formulation Deligne–Mumford era
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller groups of type (1,1))

ideas.what: Legendre λ-map D → P^1\{0,1,∞} ≃ M_{1,1}[2]', equivariant along PSL(2,Z) → SL(2,F_2) ≃ S_3, with kernel the free group π_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: λ-function / Γ(2) uniformization; M_{0,4}/S_3 versus M_{1,1}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (relation between the (0,4) and (1,1) levels of the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Mixed (equivariant) fundamental group of the multiplicity (U_{0,3}, S_3) at a point with nontrivial stabilizer, here the Z/3-fixed point e^{iπ/3}
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of a quotient stack/orbifold at a stacky point; mixed π_1 of an étale groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 framework), Noohi and others for stacks
ideas.where_published: Ideas present in La Longue Marche; explicit treatment unsure

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, classical identification (λ-function, Γ(2), PSL(2,Z) as orbifold π_1 of P^1\{0,1,∞}//S_3) phrased in Grothendieck's language of multiplicities. It is useful for base-point bookkeeping in his Galois–Teichmüller programme but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
